rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a multimodal setup with advanced RNA (scvi_n200) and image (resnet50) encoders, weighted fusion, and singleprofile. This balances exploration of key components (encoders, fusion) while keeping costs moderate. It addresses uncertainty about whether multimodal approaches outperform rna_only baselines and provides early insights into effective fusion strategies.

The existing evidence shows that config_026 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + weighted fusion) achieved 54% validation accuracy. This experiment will test replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (a more complex model) while keeping the image encoder and fusion method the same. This clarifies whether the RNA encoder choice significantly impacts performance. scgpt may offer better representation power, and the cost is expected to be similar to config_026 (both use resnet50 and weighted fusion). This balances exploration of key components with exploitation of a promising direction.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder with weighted fusion (config_026) achieves 0.5399 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to concat fusion (config_004) could improve performance while keeping the same RNA/image encoders. It clarifies the optimal fusion strategy for this encoder pair, balancing exploration of architectural variations with low cost (expected ~0.59 GPU hours).

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder and weighted fusion achieves 0.54 accuracy. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with a more complex imagenet_vit_l image encoder while keeping the RNA encoder and fusion method consistent. This clarifies whether advanced image encoders improve performance, building on the current best setup. The expected cost is higher (approx 1.2 GPU hours) but justified by the potential impact of the image encoder choice.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with weighted fusion (config_003) achieves 0.5375 validation accuracy. This experiment tests the impact of switching to concat fusion with the same RNA and image encoders, which could clarify if fusion method improvements can surpass the current best. It is a cost-effective choice (estimated ~0.53 GPU hours) that directly builds on the top-performing configuration.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50/image encoder, and weighted fusion achieve ~0.54 accuracy. This experiment tests using a more powerful image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) with transformer aggregation on multiprofile data, which could improve accuracy by leveraging stronger feature extraction and complex interactions. It addresses uncertainty around the impact of ViT image encoders and transformer aggregation on multiprofile settings, balancing exploration of advanced architectures with the potential for higher accuracy. Expected cost is ~1.2-1.5 GPU hours, justified by the potential performance gain over existing ~0.59 GPU hour configurations.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_010) achieve the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests a similar setup with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder, which balances cost and performance. The expected cost is ~3.0 GPU hours, staying within budget while exploring a promising direction.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_010) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests a similar setup but with pca_n2000 RNA encoder (cheaper than scvi_n200) to reduce training cost while maintaining the effective aggregation and fusion strategy. It clarifies if the RNA encoder complexity impacts performance without sacrificing accuracy, balancing exploration and exploitation under the remaining budget.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using transformer aggregation (e.g., config_010 with 0.725 accuracy) outperform others. This experiment tests a similar setup (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l) with concat fusion instead of weighted fusion, clarifying whether fusion type impacts performance. It’s a logical extension of the top-performing config_010, with expected cost ~3.6 GPU hours (similar to config_010), balancing exploitation of known strengths and exploration of fusion method variations.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_010) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.7249). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, a logical extension of the top-performing config_010. The scgpt encoder may offer better representation capabilities, and this configuration clarifies if combining it with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion improves accuracy further. The expected cost is ~4.5 GPU hours, which is reasonable for the remaining budget.
